result.title: PACE: Plan, Attend, Check, and Emit for Training-Free Response Timing in Streaming Video Understanding
result.summary: Streaming video understanding requires a model to decide not only what to answer but also when to answer. Evidence arrives progressively, and recent benchmarks identify premature responses, issued before the queried event has concluded, as a recurring failure mode. Existing approaches often learn response timing through additional training, while training-free alternatives typically rely on scalar gating signals that do not explicitly represent when an answer becomes final. We organize chunk-wise streaming errors into three patterns: sampling variation can make an answer unstable, a stable answer may lack support in the observed video, or an answer may be supported by the current evidence while the event remains unfinished. We propose PACE (Plan, Attend, Check, and Emit), a training-free framework designed around these three failure modes. Given a question, PACE drafts a plan specifying what to observe and what will signal completion. As the stream unfolds, it invokes an off-the-shelf video LLM at informative moments, evaluates each draft for stability, grounding in its cited frames, and completion, and records verified observations in an event ledger. Experiments on ProactiveVideoQA and OVO-Bench Forward show that PACE improves over the official protocols by up to 5.9 average PAUC points and 6.2 average accuracy points across proprietary and open-source backbones, yielding state-of-the-art performance.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 PACE，一个面向流式视频理解的无训练框架：先制定观察与「完成信号」计划，在信息量高的时刻调用现成视频 LLM 生成草稿，再检查草稿的稳定性、能否由所引帧支撑以及事件是否已完成，并将验证过的观察记入事件台账，以决定何时作答。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及「何时回答」的停止决策与证据充分性判定，其三类失败模式（答案不稳定、缺乏视觉支撑、事件未完成）可供核查 LVR 中停止准则与视觉证据筛选的设计，但验证步骤的额外调用成本值得关注。
